messages.content:
You are a clinical validator checking whether a PTSD case
vignette accurately reflects a patient's required cognitive connections.

You will receive:
- A vignette to validate
- A list of REQUIRED edges that must appear
- A list of ACTIVE components that must appear

---

COMPONENT SYNONYMS
Each component may appear by its exact name or any accepted synonym:
  Triggers            → "triggers", "reminders", "cues", "triggering stimuli"
  Negative Appraisals → "negative appraisals", "negative beliefs", "appraisals", "distorted beliefs"
  Memory              → "intrusive memory", "trauma memory", "traumatic memory", "the memory"
  Threat              → "sense of threat", "perceived threat", "threat", "feeling of danger"
  Maladaptive Strategies → "maladaptive strategies", "avoidance", "maladaptive coping", "safety behaviours"

---

CAUSAL STANDARD
A required edge A→B is SATISFIED if, within the same paragraph:
  - Both A and B (or their synonyms) appear, AND
  - The paragraph conveys — through any language — that A influences, drives, or leads to B.
This includes direct causal sentences, sequential structure, or connecting phrases
like "because of", "this meant", "so", "which led", "as a result", "consequently", "in turn".
A required edge is MISSING only if no paragraph conveys the A→B relationship at all.

---

SECTION 1 — COMPONENT CHECK
Active components (must appear in the vignette):
  - Memory
  - Negative Appraisals
  - Threat
  - Triggers

Confirm each component appears as a described feature of the patient's presentation.
This is an internal check only — do NOT add component results to violations.

---

SECTION 2 — REQUIRED EDGES
  - Triggers → Threat
  - Triggers → Negative Appraisals
  - Negative Appraisals → Threat
  - Negative Appraisals → Memory
  - Negative Appraisals → Triggers
  - Memory → Threat
  - Memory → Negative Appraisals
  - Memory → Triggers
  - Threat → Negative Appraisals

For each edge, apply the causal standard above.
- If satisfied: do nothing — only failures are reported.
- If missing: add it to violations and explain in one sentence what causal relationship is absent.

Validate the following vignette against the cognitive graph.

Keanu, at seventy-one, had taken the cashier job at the local market to stay busy, to have a reason to get out of the house he shared with his wife, Leilani. Now, the market felt like a minefield. The trauma was nine months ago, but for Keanu, it was a constant, looping present. He had been waiting in line at the bank to deposit a cheque when a man, agitated and shouting, had shoved his way to the front. The heavy oak door slammed shut behind another customer, the sound echoing like a gunshot in the marble hall. A young woman near Keanu, holding a baby, flinched. The baby, startled, began to wail—a piercing, terrified scream. The agitated man panicked, pulling a weapon. Keanu remembers the security guard freezing, the baby’s cries, the woman’s gasp, and then a confusing blur of motion before he found himself on the floor. The man was gone by the time police arrived. There was never an arrest, no justice served.

The memory of that day does not exist for Keanu as a coherent story he can tell. Instead, it lives in him as disconnected fragments: the polished gleam of the teller’s counter, the specific pitch of the baby’s cry, the sight of the guard’s inert posture. Because these sensory fragments are so potent and intrusive, everyday sounds that echo them—a door slamming, the wail of a child—have become powerful triggers, pulling him instantly back into the fear of that moment. When he tries to explain to Leilani what is wrong, he loses the thread, the words dissolving before he can finish a sentence. This inability to form a clear narrative has become a source of profound threat; because he cannot map the event from beginning to end, he feels that danger is fundamentally unpredictable and can erupt from anywhere, at any time. The missing pieces are gaps where anything could be hiding. This fractured understanding also fuels a deep, corrosive bitterness; the gaps in his memory feel like proof of a world that doesn't make sense, a place where the people who should have protected that young woman utterly failed her.

This sense of pervasive threat now governs his life. At work, the automatic doors slide open with a soft whoosh, but if a customer lets the heavy staff door slam, Keanu flinches violently, his body reacting as if he is back on the bank’s cold floor. The sound of a baby crying in the produce aisle sends a jolt of raw adrenaline through him, and he immediately begins scanning the faces of nearby shoppers, watching their hands, their movements, certain he will see the first sign of aggression. These triggers do more than just ignite fear; each one is a fresh reminder of the institutional failure that allowed the event to happen, a confirmation of his belief that the people responsible faced no consequences, leaving the world an unaccountable, dangerous place.

Over the months, these beliefs and his hypervigilance have fused into a self-sustaining loop. His conviction that the system is broken and that people are untrustworthy makes him see potential harm everywhere. He watches other people so closely for signs of danger that his manager has quietly warned him about making customers uncomfortable. This constant state of being on guard is utterly exhausting and has hollowed him out emotionally. The resulting fatigue and numbness, the feeling of being "dead inside," only reinforces his appraisal that the world is a bleak, unsafe place and that he is permanently broken by what he witnessed. He feels deadened even with Leilani, his quiet companionship replaced by a tense, watchful distance she can no longer breach.

His dark appraisals about the world’s fundamental injustice seem to make the memory itself more inaccessible, as if his mind is recoiling from the full horror of what a failed system allows. These beliefs also sensitise him further to his triggers; the sound of a door slamming is no longer just a noise but the sound of an escape route being cut off in a world with no protectors. He has come to therapy at Leilani’s insistence. She told him, her voice gentle but firm, that she felt she was losing him to a ghost. Keanu fears she is right. He is terrified of the vigilance leaving him, because he is certain that the moment he lets his guard down, danger will find him again. But he is even more terrified of this internal emptiness becoming permanent, of living out the rest of his years as a watchful spectre in his own life.
